title: Best GPS Watches for Running and Hiking
excerpt: GPS watches for trail running and hiking, from the Garmin Enduro 3 and Coros Apex 4 to the Suunto Vertical 2, compared on battery, navigation and price.
body:
Best GPS Watches for Running and Hiking

Updated November 2026. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update; retailers often sell for less.

A watch for running and hiking needs more battery and better navigation than a road running watch. These picks are ranked by how far from a charger they can take you. Prices are US list prices (MSRP), and battery figures are the manufacturers' ratings.

The picks

Garmin Enduro 3: longest battery

The Garmin Enduro 3 launched at $899. It's rated for 120 hours of GPS, or 60 hours in all-systems multi-band mode. With enough sun on its solar lens, Garmin rates it for up to 320 hours of GPS. It suits multi-day trips and 100-mile races.

Coros Apex 4: best all-round trail watch

The Coros Apex 4 lists at $479 for the 46 mm model, or $429 for the 42 mm. The 46 mm version is rated for 65 hours of all-systems GPS, or 41 hours in its most accurate dual-frequency mode.

Suunto Vertical 2: long battery with an AMOLED screen

The Suunto Vertical 2 lists at $599 in steel, or $699 in titanium. Suunto rates it for 65 hours of continuous dual-band GPS recording and 20 days as a smartwatch.

Garmin Instinct 3 Solar: rugged and simple

The Garmin Instinct 3 Solar lists at $399 for the 45 mm model. It has a tough case, a memory-in-pixel display and solar charging. It's a good fit for hikers who want a simple, button-operated watch with solar top-ups.

Garmin Forerunner 970: best for runners who want maps

The Garmin Forerunner 970 lists at $749.99. It's rated for 26 hours in GPS-only mode and has offline maps, making it a running-first watch that can still navigate trails.

Garmin Forerunner 170: entry level

The Garmin Forerunner 170 lists at $299.99 and is rated for 20 hours in GPS-only mode. That covers day hikes and races up to about a 50K for most runners. It isn't enough for a 100-mile race or a multi-day trip without recharging.

Features that matter for hiking

  • Battery for your longest day: estimate your longest time out, add a margin, and check the watch's rating in the GPS mode you'll actually use.
  • Navigation: breadcrumb routes show the line to follow, while full offline maps show the terrain around you. Check which one a watch has before you buy.
  • Barometric altimeter: it gives steadier elevation readings than GPS alone.
  • Multi-band GPS: it helps in canyons and dense forest, at the cost of battery life.

FAQ

Is a running watch good enough for hiking?

For day hikes, yes. For multi-day trips, you need either a battery-focused watch, such as the Garmin Enduro 3 or Coros Apex 4, or a way to recharge.
